clue.text: Pay by a quarter to eight

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass
a rowing eight is the boat's crew

explanation.surface: Someone is told they will be paid at a quarter to eight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter to eight' looks like a time; it is S (a compass quarter) put before CREW (a rowing eight). SCREW is old British slang for wages.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a worker's wages are their screw, so the word is a noun for pay.

clue.text: One who cares to make an offer

definitions.meaning: someone who looks after others, as a carer or nurse does
to put in a formal bid for a contract

explanation.surface: A carer who also puts in bids.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is one who tends or looks after, and to tender is to submit a formal bid.

definitions.meaning: a domestic heater full of hot water
the part of a car engine that keeps it from overheating

explanation.surface: A choice between something that heats and something that chills.
explanation.definitionFit: A household radiator heats a room, while a car's radiator dissipates engine heat to keep it cool.

clue.text: I'd come up with poetry that's different

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word I'd is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the contraction I'd, here as its two letters
poetry is verse

explanation.surface: Someone claims their poems are unlike anyone else's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come up' turns ID into DI, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverse things vary from one another, so the word is a synonym for differing or varied.

parts.note: a bill is a banknote
a hook catches the eye in a hook-and-eye fastening

explanation.surface: Advice on a striking new tool for the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eye-catching' looks like 'striking'; it means the hook of a hook-and-eye fastener on clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A billhook is a curved-bladed tool used by gardeners and hedgers for cutting branches.

clue.text: Parson promises to pay for someone else

parts.note: a parson is a vicar, a parish priest
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A clergyman signs IOUs on another person's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vicarious is experienced or done in place of another person, by proxy.

indicators.note: arranged signals that the letters of the word catechism are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A religious catechism is laid out in a planned order.
explanation.definitionFit: A schematic layout is drawn as a diagram or plan, so it follows a scheme.

clue.text: Imitate one in opera hitting a note

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Boheme
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: An opera singer copies another while hitting a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in opera' looks like the letter I inside a word; it is the character Mimi, with 'hitting' just placing C beside her.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic someone is to copy their manner or voice.

parts.note: read not as a sharp remark but as the mark left behind after a cut to the skin

explanation.surface: A sharp note to jog someone's memory.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a lasting mark on the skin that recalls an old wound.

clue.text: Telephone fault may mean a reporter missing it

definitions.meaning: a phone with no dial tone because the connection is broken
the time limit a journalist fails to meet for filing copy

explanation.surface: A broken phone could make a journalist late with a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead line is a telephone with no signal, and a deadline is the time by which copy must be filed.

parts.note: suggests a salt mine, but means a basement room, the salt version being a table shaker

explanation.surface: Asking where salt is mined underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar is a room below ground level, and a salt cellar is the small dish holding salt at table.

indicators.note: without means the hesitation sound is taken out of the word for an author

parts.note: an author is a writer
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A court order is served on a novelist who does not hesitate.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a written court order, such as one summoning someone to appear.

clue.text: Like one treating Ida with scorn?

definitions.text: Like one treating Ida with scorn?

indicators.note: treating suggests processing, so the letters of Ida and scorn are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Describing someone who looks down on a woman named Ida.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treating' shuffles IDA and SCORN together; the whole clue then also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sardonic person is mocking and scornful in manner.

clue.text: Dine with Ralph, prepared to flirt

indicators.note: prepared hints at something made ready, here the letters of dine and Ralph made into a new order

explanation.surface: Ralph comes to dinner ready to chat someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to have casual affairs or play around with women, a verb for flirting.

clue.text: Strange charm that is pure fantasy

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd or out of place, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: An odd allure that turns out to be imaginary.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is an illusion or wild fancy, named after a mythical monster.

parts.note: not the French dish but a word that names both a kind of duck and a kind of citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A menu offering duck with orange sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandarin is both an ornamental Asian duck and a small loose-skinned citrus fruit.

definitions.meaning: escorted someone on an outing, as on a date

explanation.surface: Someone went on a date and was then taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone out is to go on a date with them, and to take something out is to remove it.

explanation.surface: The Spectator described as a weekly magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spectator is itself a British weekly magazine, which makes the surface misleading; the answer is the Observer, a British Sunday paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An observer is one who watches, and The Observer is a newspaper printed each Sunday.

parts.note: a head is a principal, as of a school
a way is a method

explanation.surface: The main way to get ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Making headway means moving forward, especially slowly or against difficulty.

clue.text: When alone, get changed and stretch out

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of alone and get take a different order

explanation.surface: Instructions to change clothes and do some stretching when by yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate is to lengthen or extend something.

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of bale are disordered, put out of place

explanation.surface: Someone is able to bail out or a hay bale can be put out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able to do something means one can do it.

parts.note: read as a pit where surplus or drained oil collects, not a gusher in the ground

explanation.surface: An unwanted oil well.
explanation.definitionFit: A sump is the reservoir under an engine, or any pit into which excess liquid drains.

indicators.note: interrupts means a boy breaks into the word my, sitting between its letters

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone's complaint is cut short by a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupts' signals the container: the boy breaks into the word 'my', so 'complaint' is the definition, not part of the surface grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is an illness, and a complaint is also an ailment.

clue.text: Lower a boat with a number

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed boat
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Instructions to let down a boat carrying a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' looks like let down; it rhymes with flower and means to frown.
explanation.definitionFit: To lour or lower is to look angry and sullen, as a scowl does.

indicators.note: perhaps hints that in late is only one possible order of these letters

explanation.surface: Being late might be unavoidable.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to involve it as a necessary consequence.

definitions.meaning: a vessel left adrift at sea by its crew

explanation.surface: An order for the crew to leave their vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A derelict building is neglected and deserted, and a derelict is a vessel left by its crew.

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsy disorder, so the letters of being are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting started can be difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin is to commence or set off.

explanation.surface: Something noted as having been taken apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Words taken down are written as notes, and a structure taken down has been disassembled.
